PullRequest.Title: agentHost: avoid error for tool completion after cancellation
PullRequest.Body:
I generated this by scanning my logs, pls take if it's good/useful

---
🤖 

## Summary

- treat an in-flight tool completion after cancellation as an expected race
- keep dropping the late completion, but log it at trace level instead of error
- preserve error logging for unexpected stale provider output
- add focused regression coverage for cancellation quarantine

## Context

Recent Agent Host logs reported expected tool completions as errors after a session was cancelled:

```text
tool.execution_complete emitted after cancellation; dropping
```

Tools that were already running can complete while cancellation is being processed. The completion still must not mutate the cancelled turn, but this race is not itself an error.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "(quarantines late cancelled events|traces dropped in-flight tool completions)"` (2 passing)
- pre-commit hygiene check

Scenarios.Scenario: A user cancels an active Copilot agent turn while one or more root tool calls are still running, and their SDK tool.execution_complete events arrive after cancellation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The cancellation request waits on the existing wrapper.session.abort() call. Late tool-completion handling occurs afterward and is not required for cancellation or the next turn to progress; each completion performs existing cleanup/telemetry checks, then the changed helper emits one trace instead of one error and returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke and await the provider SDK session abort.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider abort call was awaited before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This existing call is the cancellation critical path; late completion logging runs only after independently arriving SDK events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit telemetry for a successful eligible SQL tool completion after parsing its query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one telemetry submission per successful SQL tool completion; non-SQL tools return without submission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same telemetry check and submission occurred before the late-event gate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously in the completion callback before the cancellation-drop check, but late completion processing is off the user-visible cancellation critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the late-completion diagnostic to the log service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One diagnostic per dropped late tracked root tool completion; effective cardinality is the number of root tools still completing after the abort.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Previously the same event constructed the same message and made one error-level log call; the diff changes that one call to trace level only for tool completions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous in the late SDK event callback but not on cancellation progress; it does not block the next turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales linearly with the number of tracked root tool completions that race with an abort; the diff does not increase that count or add work per completion. Existing SQL telemetry parsing additionally scales with query length, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The SDK may deliver completions for multiple in-flight tools, but each event invokes one synchronous JavaScript handler with no new Promise.all, queue, limiter, or concurrency burst. Effective work remains one handler and one drop log per late tracked root completion, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or negative cache participates. The boolean cancellation quarantine is checked independently for every completion before and after the diff; there is no cache key, miss behavior, or coalescing change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High. The changed call site passes a constant flag only to the late root tool-completion case, while every other call keeps the default. The helper still constructs one identical message and invokes one logger method when quarantining; no new boundary, retained state, batching change, or eager work is added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The typical number of simultaneously in-flight root tools and logging backend configuration vary, but this does not affect causality: the diff preserves one log call per late completion and generally lowers its enabled severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The only production behavior change replaces an error-level log with a trace-level log at unchanged cardinality, while normal non-cancelled completions return before message allocation. The added test runs only in the test suite.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. Traced cancellation state, tool-completion event wiring, cleanup, telemetry, logging, and test-only work. The PR neither adds nor amplifies a performance mechanism; it lowers the severity of an existing one-per-late-completion diagnostic.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
